B.13     Ordinary relative one-forms on the actual local models
The following computation concerns the relative cotangent module on the smooth total space,
before restriction to a fibre. All base maps and local rings are specified in the statement.

Proposition B.35 (crossing and multiple-fibre modules). The symbols R2 and R3 denote
copies of the same regular local ring, with different maps from the one-dimensional base: let
R2 = C{x, y, z} with base coordinate t = xy, and let R3 = C{x, y, z} with base coordinate t = xyz.
Then
                                            R2 dx ⊕ R2 dy ⊕ R2 dz
                         M2 := Ω1R2 /C{t} =                        ,
                                               R2 (y dx + x dy)
                                                                                          (W.176)
                                              R3 dx ⊕ R3 dy ⊕ R3 dz
                         M3 := Ω1R3 /C{t} =                             .
                                            R3 (yz dx + xz dy + xy dz)
Both modules are torsion-free, but neither is locally free at the origin. They embed in free modules
by
        M2 ,→ R2 e ⊕ R2 dz, dx 7−→ xe, dy 7−→ −ye, dz 7−→ dz,
                                                                                             (W.177)
        M3 ,→ R3 e1 ⊕ R3 e2 , dx 7−→ xe1 , dy 7−→ ye2 , dz 7−→ −z(e1 + e2 ),
with images
                        R2 dz ⊕ (x, y)e,     R3 xe1 + R3 ye2 + R3 z(e1 + e2 ).                (W.178)
If Rm = C{s, y1 , y2 } and the base coordinate is t = sm with m ≥ 2, then

                          Ω1Rm /C{t} ≃ Rm dy1 ⊕ Rm dy2 ⊕ Rm /(sm−1 ) ds,                      (W.179)

and the final summand is exactly its torsion submodule.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and
calculations in the proof.

Proof. Differentiating the three equations gives the presentations in (W.176). For M2 , the
first map in (W.177) sends (a, b, c) to (ax − by, c). If this is zero, then c = 0 and ax = by.
Since x and y are relatively prime in the UFD R2 , there is an h with b = xh and a = yh;
hence its kernel is exactly the displayed relation. For M3 , the second map sends (a, b, c) to
(ax − cz, by − cz). If it is zero, relative primeness first gives x | c, then y | (c/x); writing c = xyh
gives (a, b, c) = h(yz, xz, xy), again exactly the defining relation. Thus both maps are injective,
proving torsion-freeness and (W.178).
    At the maximal ideal (x, y, z) each defining relation has all coefficients in that maximal ideal.
Consequently the quotient of either module by the maximal ideal has dimension 3 over C, while
its generic rank is 2; a locally free module of rank 2 would need only 2 generators. This proves
non-local-freeness at the origin. Finally, for t = sm one has dt = msm−1 ds = 0 relatively. The
integer m is a unit in C, so the decomposition (W.179) follows. Its last summand is annihilated
by sm−1 , while the other two summands are free; after inverting s it vanishes. It is therefore
exactly the torsion submodule.

Remark B.36 (scope of the local correction). The modules in (W.176) are modules on the
smooth total-space chart, and their torsion-freeness is asserted before restricting to a fibre.
They must be distinguished both from the intrinsic sheaf Ω1S of the singular fibre and from
the restricted relative module Mi ⊗Ri Ri /(t) (i = 2, 3): tensoring with the fibre ring can create
conductor-supported torsion, as the τ calculation in the proof of Theorem 5.8 shows. If a local
quotient is finite surjective étale over a chart in (W.179), relative differentials commute with
this base change and faithful flatness then reflects torsion of the pulled-back module; a ramified
quotient requires a separate invariant-module calculation. Thus the bare t = xyz chart has a
torsion-free but non-locally-free total-space relative module for p = 1; this fact alone does not

                                                  600
Torus-fibred compact complex threefolds                                                         Paper II


decide torsion after fibre restriction or quotient. The
                                                    V multiple-fibre charts do have the total-space
torsion in (W.179). No claim about torsion in 2 Ω1 or 3 Ω1 , and no global direct-image or
                                                           V
Hodge conclusion, is made here.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; equation (W.176); proposition 5.8;
equation (W.179).

D    Programs, certificates and reproducible commands
Paths are relative to the companion archive. Change to the stated working directory and
execute the displayed command. The calculations use Python 3, with SymPy and mpmath
where imported. Every named program and its output are retained. The individual proofs
state the exact finite rank, Smith form, polynomial identity, local character, lattice or bounded
enumeration checked. No such certificate substitutes for the complete analytic occurrence or
properness proof. A finite list of examples is never extrapolated to an unbounded parameter;
the corresponding symbolic argument is printed. The unchanged source output of d_comb.py
retains an obsolete open Kuranishi-status field. The full period-section proof in proposition 15.10
settles that question; the finite program checks its displayed degrees and dimensions and makes
no obstruction calculation.

Part I
Questions not established by the present
arguments
Open problem D.1 (The remaining comb bundle splitting). The integer m and the stated
limiting data do not determine in this paper the splitting of the rank-three bundle Km in (E.6),
or its exact number of sections. This splitting calculation is unfinished. The Kuranishi germ and
its vanishing obstruction map are established by Proposition 15.10. The four tangent cohomology
dimensions themselves are fully determined by Proposition 15.10.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; equation (E.6); proposition 15.10;
equation (E.4a); equation (E.5); equation (E.7).

The remaining finite data and the computations made. If em is the length of coker κ1 in (E.6),
then its source has rank four and degree −2, its target is OB (2m), and

                                    deg Km = −2m − 2 + em .                                  (E.7)

The degree −2 follows from the two pairs of opposite stabilizer characters of Em ∗ ⊗ G ; its root
                                                                                       m
determinant is trivial, and each finite root point subtracts one from the coarse determinant.
Although (E.4a) determines the tangent dimensions independently of the individual zeros of the
Kodaira–Spencer determinant, the support and elementary divisors of Qm still depend on that
period-section map. The tangent dimensions alone do not determine obstruction maps. The
complete period-section family and its tangent isomorphism in Proposition 15.10 establish that
the Kuranishi ideal is zero.
    We evaluated the universal exact degree and dimension expressions for m = 12, 13, 20, 100
in d_exact.py and d_comb.py; the first case already gives h1,1 ≥ 49, h1,2 ≥ 48, h0 (T ) = 25,
h1 (T ) = 97 and h2 (T ) = 73. The smallest undecided instance is the splitting of (E.6) for one
specified smoothed 12-tooth period section. The attached construction supplies an existence
argument and an open set of smoothing choices, not the transition matrices of a uniquely specified
X12 . We have not chosen and solved its nonlinear period-section smoothing equations, and
have not run two numerical methods on those missing matrices. Formulas (E.5)–(E.7) and the
growth bounds are proved, but they are not replacements for that remaining bundle-splitting
calculation.

Bounds obtained from all possible coarse splittings.            The available bundle data give the
further bounds

   0 ≤ h0 (Km ) ≤ 2m + 2,       4m + 1 ≤ h1,1 (Xm ) ≤ 6m + 3,       4m ≤ h1,2 (Xm ) ≤ 6m + 2.

Here is a complete derivation. Put S = 2m − 1, and write

              Vc = ρ∗ Em = O(a) ⊕ O(S − a),          Gc = ρ∗ Gm = O(b) ⊕ O(S − b).

The already proved nonnegative splitting implies 0 ≤ a, b ≤ S. Reordering each pair gives
a, b ≤ S/2. Taking invariants defines a natural injective morphism

                               ρ∗ Hom(Em , Gm ) −→ Hom(Vc , Gc ).

It is an isomorphism away from the two stack points, and its source is torsion free, which proves
injectivity. In the invariant local bases, the map from the nontrivial-character source line to the

                                               647
Torus-fibred compact complex threefolds                                                    Paper II


trivial-character target line has to vanish at the stack point; the other entries have no additional
condition. Thus there is one elementary condition at each finite point, consistently with the
source degree −2 in (E.7).
    The four contributions to h0 (Hom(Vc , Gc )) are

       max{b − a + 1, 0},     S − a − b + 1,    max{a + b − S + 1, 0},    max{a − b + 1, 0}.

If a + b < S, the third is zero and their sum is at most S − a − b + 1 + |a − b| + 2 ≤ S + 3. If
a + b = S, the two inequalities a, b ≤ S/2 imply a = b = S/2, and the sum is four, also at most
S + 3. Since Km is a subbundle of ρ∗ Hom(Em , Gm ), this proves h0 (Km ) ≤ S + 3 = 2m + 2.
Substitution in (E.5) proves the two Hodge bounds. In particular 0 ≤ h0 (K12 ) ≤ 26. No balanced
splitting has been assumed, and these bounds are not asserted to be sharp.

Why the numerical constraints do not determine the answer. Set D = O⊕2 ⊕ O(−1)⊕2
and L = O(2m) on P1 , with homogeneous coordinates [X : Y ]. The two morphisms

                φA = (X 2m , Y 2m , 0, 0),     φB = (0, 0, X 2m+1 , Y 2m+1 ) : D −→ L

are surjective, because their two nonzero entries have no common projective zero. The degree-2m
pencil sequence, together with the unused summands, gives

                                   ker φA = O(−2m) ⊕ O(−1)⊕2 .

The degree-(2m + 1) pencil sequence tensored by O(−1) gives

                                    ker φB = O⊕2 ⊕ O(−2m − 2).

Both maps therefore have rank-four source of degree −2, target of degree 2m, and cokernel of
length zero. Their rank-three kernels both have degree −2m − 2, but their section dimensions
are zero and two. For m = 12 the splitting triples are (−24, −1, −1) and (0, 0, −26). These exact
vector-bundle examples show that the known rank, degree and cokernel length alone cannot
determine the kernel. We do not assert that either morphism is the cup map of an admissible
comb period section, or that different such geometric sections have different Hodge numbers.
    The retained invariant homology and cohomology classes do not remove this missing
information. They supply sections of Em and Gm , and their tensor belongs to Em ⊗ Gm . The
cotangent kernel instead involves Em ∗ ⊗ G ; there is no specified identification of E with E ∗ .
                                           m                                          m        m
Likewise the exact tangent calculation uses a different cup map. An actual admissible period
section, its transition matrices and its derivative are required to decide the remaining kernel.
The existence and smoothing construction supplies an open set of such sections, rather than
coefficient data selecting a unique one. The estimates and the algebraic examples above do not
substitute for solving that geometric choice and its cup-map calculation.
